title: A potato price gap that outlasted modeled costs
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, January 2023: a ₹820 per quintal median price gap on 18 matched days. After modeled costs: ₹421 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2023: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 18 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: January 2023
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 18 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹695 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,500 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹820/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹820 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: ₹421 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes ₹274 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 18 of 18 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 18 of 18 days, averaging ₹411 per quintal; 0 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Even under the stress test, the modeled median stayed positive. It is still a historical model, not proof a trade happened or would work today.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹273/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: Even under the stress test, the modeled median stayed positive. It is still a historical model, not proof a trade happened or would work today.

title: The potato storage gamble
summary: Agra potatoes: ₹658 in March 2023, ₹860 in October. Break-even storage budget: ₹96 per quintal.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the yearly harvest-to-autumn storage question at Agra, with 9 earlier seasons to learn from.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of Agra daily modal prices (≥8 reports)
caveats: No cold-storage rent is cited, so no net profit is claimed.
Stored and fresh potatoes may differ in grade.

scenes.headline: March 2023
scenes.caption: Potatoes are harvested in early spring and often held in cold stores in western Uttar Pradesh, which the RBI paper calls the potato belt's key selling point.

scenes.headline: Harvest price
scenes.caption: Agra's March 2023 median: ₹658 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The informed bet
scenes.caption: Using only the 9 earlier years, March→October had averaged +₹422. A rule-following trader would store.

scenes.headline: October 2023
scenes.caption: October median: ₹860, a change of +30.8%.

scenes.headline: Shrinkage and interest
scenes.caption: Allowing 7% loss and 12% a year interest for 7 months leaves a storage budget of ₹96 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹96 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.

assumptions.value: not in cited evidence; shown as break-even budget

conclusion: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹96 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.

scenes.headline: November 2023
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 28 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹810 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,150 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹325/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹325 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹60 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹186 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 6 of 28 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 3 of 28 days, averaging −₹52 per quintal; 2 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: The ₹325 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.
